summary: Elevated 5xx after edge XDP packet-drop rule rollout triggering upstream runtime respawn loop
description:
Issue summary:
During a canary rollout of a new XDP packet-drop ACL on our edge load balancers (us-west), we started to observe a rise in 5xx responses for customer traffic (notably embedding uploads and long-poll chat sessions). The spike began ~2026-03-12T08:10Z shortly after the rollout window.

Impact:
- Elevated 5xx rate across two customer tenants (LumenAI and several self-serve customers) with error rate rising from baseline ~0.2% to ~6% for a 40-minute window.
- Customers reported aborted streaming sessions and failed embedding uploads.
- Some upstream serving-runtime processes entered a restart loop (watchdog-triggered respawn) causing additional capacity instability.

Environment:
- Pod: api-gateway -> edge LB (xdp-canned-rules) -> runtime-proxy -> serving-runtime (gpu pool).
- Regions: prod/us-west primary, spillover to us-east observed.
- Timeframe: 2026-03-12 08:10Z — ongoing (investigating).

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Canary apply XDP rule that drops UDP/TCP packets matching sample rate and large payloads on edge LB.
2) Send mixed workload: small chat requests (HTTP/2 streaming) + large embedding uploads (multi-part).
3) Observe increased TCP retransmits at edge and stream RST/half-close events on api-gateway -> runtime.
4) Upstream runtimes log watchdog timeouts and respawn.

Observed metrics/log snippets:
- apigw 5xx rate: baseline 0.2% -> 6.1% between 08:12-08:52Z.
- kernel (edge LB) dmesg: "xdp: packet_drop rule hit (rule-id=17) src=... count=3121" repeated.
- netstat on edge proxy: high SYN_RECV and retransmit counters increased by 4000 in 10m.
- runtime logs (serving-runtime): "watchdog: worker pid=4921 unresponsive, restarting" followed by GPU warmup logs and delayed ready state.
- api-gateway logs: several HTTP/2 stream reset frames followed by 502/503 returned to client.

Notes: initial rollout used conservative sampling but coincided with embedding batch uploads which amplified retransmits and produced many half-closed streams. This triggered a pattern where runtime workers observed intermittent connection failures and the supervisor triggered restarts; restarts cause GPU warmup and short capacity drop, which increased 5xx amplification in a feedback loop.
comments: Support (2026-03-12T08:25Z) - Maya Patel: Customer LumenAI reported elevated 5xx and failed embedding uploads. Collected request IDs and timestamps; escalated to SRE. Linked logs attached in ticket.
SRE (2026-03-12T08:40Z) - Ethan Collins: Observed XDP drop counters increasing on edge LB canary nodes. Kicked off correlation between drop spikes and 5xx timeline. Adding network team.
Network (2026-03-12T09:05Z) - Karen Liu: Canary XDP config was rolled at 08:05Z with rule-id=17 (drop-on-large-payload-sample). Rolling back canary to baseline on two affected nodes now.
Customer (LumenAI) (2026-03-12T09:12Z) - Alex Moretti: Thanks — our ingestion jobs coincided with your deployment window. We can throttle uploads for a window if helpful.

SRE (2026-03-12T09:33Z) - Ethan Collins: After rollback on canary nodes, edge drop counters returned to baseline and 5xx rate dropped to ~0.6% within two minutes. Runtime respawn frequency reduced. Continuing monitoring and gathering artifacts for root cause.
investigation_notes:
2026-03-12 08:10Z correlation: first 5xx uptick matched XDP canary application at 08:05Z.
Evidence: time-aligned dmesg xdp entries and apigw error histograms.

Packet-level analysis: increased TCP retransmit and RTT spike between client and edge; many streams saw HTTP/2 RST_STREAM. Not typical for pure runtime OOMs.
Action: pulled tcpdump from edge and compared to client traces from LumenAI — retransmits correspond to dropped packets at XDP layer.

Runtime behavior: serving-runtime's watchdog threshold was 6s for unresponsive worker; intermittent network-induced stalls caused the watchdog to treat worker as dead and respawn. Respawn sequence triggers GPU reinitialize (~3-7s), which leads to transient capacity loss.
Hypothesis: network packet drops cause application-level streaming stalls and the runtime watchdog is too aggressive for network-induced stalls.

Repro steps validated in staging: applying similar XDP rule to staging edge replicated 5xx spike when combined with concurrent large embedding uploads. Increasing watchdog threshold prevented respawn but allowed long tail latency.
root_cause: A canary XDP packet-drop ACL (rule-id=17) on edge load-balancers dropped packets for sampled large payloads. Drops caused TCP retransmits and HTTP/2 stream resets -> upstream serving-runtime interpreted repeated stalls as worker unresponsiveness and triggered watchdog-driven respawns. The respawns caused GPU warmup delays and transient capacity loss, amplifying 5xx rates in a feedback loop.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-12 09:05Z): rolled back XDP rule on canary edge nodes. Immediate drop in 5xx to near-baseline observed within 2m.

Short-term fixes deployed (2026-03-12 10:20Z): increased serving-runtime watchdog unresponsive threshold to 12s for affected pools, adjusted apigw retry and keepalive to be less aggressive against HTTP/2 stream RSTs, and added temporary admission control to throttle large embedding batch concurrency from customers in prod/us-west.

Long-term actions: 1) Network will rework XDP rule to avoid dropping packets for TCP streams with established flow (maintain per-connection allowance); 2) Add a runtime health-smoothing window to avoid respawn for transient network stalls; 3) Add observability: expose XDP drop-rate as an alert and correlate with apigw 5xx SLI; 4) Publish canary rollout checklist requiring mixed-workload soak tests.
postmortem_tasks: TICKET-1: Network to update XDP rule to use connection-aware sampling and test in staging (owner: Karen Liu).
TICKET-2: Runtime to implement respawn smoothing and histogram-based thresholds (owner: Priya Nair).
TICKET-3: Observability: create composite alert for edge-drop -> apigw-5xx correlation (owner: SRE team).
TICKET-4: Run chaos/soak with mixed embed+stream workload before future edge rollout (owner: QA/Platform).
TICKET-5: Customer follow-up and RCA summary to LumenAI (owner: CS - Maya Patel).
resolution_status: Mitigated (rollback + runtime threshold increase); follow-ups scheduled
follow_up_notes: Customer outreach: Maya to schedule RCA call with LumenAI for 2026-03-15.
Monitor: set 24h elevated-metrics watch for prod/us-west; check for any late regressions during evening traffic window.
Record: add incident to team retro and update edge rollout runbook with explicit mixed-workload test gate.
